findings: String-path overloads accept OrdinalIgnoreCase equality before shell lookup, so same spelling/case-insensitive spelling does not require source existence and is not filesystem identity or content equality. Do not adopt as exact file comparison.
PIDL comparison accepts Shell CompareIDs equal or fallback case-insensitive SHGetNameFromIDList URL equality. Shell item equivalence is intended for navigation/tab reuse, not digest/byte equality.
IsEquivalent catches exceptions and returns false, conflating lookup failure with inequality; a scanner needs separate issue evidence rather than treating unreadable source as a healthy unique file.

Temporary PIDLs are released with FreeCoTaskMem in finally blocks. Desktop shell COM pointer is released after RCW creation. Dispose releases RCW and finalizer calls Dispose; no disposed-state guard exists on comparison methods. Thread/apartment behavior remains unverified.
ParseDisplayName declaration was not inspected, so whether HRESULT failures become exceptions is not established here. No claim of a concrete unchecked-HRESULT bug.

App startup uses a named mutex to admit one instance, second instance displays information and exits. Constants define keyboard profile defaults and update URL; no hooks, updates or external operations executed.
